supporting_observations.claim: FILE-ORC-01 ran the Keystone backup agent as ORCHARD\svc-safe with a Nightly job targeting ingest.keystone-backup.net.

The proxy recorded a 640,000,000-byte client-to-server transfer through a successful CONNECT tunnel to ingest.keystone-backup.net; the corresponding connection was made by Keystone agent.exe running as svc-safe.
The observed destination, agent, service account, and transfer size match the inventory’s approved Keystone offsite backup activity, which is expected to upload several hundred MB.
The transfer records are timestamped 13:49:51 UTC, rather than around 13:46 UTC as described in the alert.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records show the large transfer at 13:49:51 UTC, not at approximately 13:46 UTC; they do not establish whether the alert timestamp reflects a different event time or clock.
The proxy records transfer volume and destination, but the supplied logs do not expose the contents of the encrypted transfer.
claims_not_established: Whether the alert timestamp of approximately 13:46 UTC is a reporting or clock discrepancy.
Whether the backed-up data included any particular files or sensitive information.
additional_evidence_needed: If exact timestamp reconciliation is required before closure, compare the original alert’s event-time basis with proxy and endpoint clock synchronization.
unrelated_findings: WS-THART-01 (help desk) established an RDP session to FILE-ORC-01; the inventory says remote administration is only performed from WS-SBYRNE-01. Review separately; this does not establish that the backup transfer was malicious. Records: T270-00010, T270-00017, T270-00021.

FILE-ORC-01 made an SSH connection to PROXY-ORC-01, a remote-access service not listed as approved. Investigate separately; this occurs after the observed backup transfer and does not decide this alert. Record: T270-00450.

A network log shows a failed SMB authentication attempt for disabled account svc_mgmt from DC-ORC-01 to FILE-ORC-01. Investigate separately; it is unrelated to the observed backup transfer. Records: T270-00447, T270-00449.
